IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR LEAVE TO APPEAL) NO. 11611 of  2015  ==========================================================
 STATE OF GUJARAT....Applicant(s)
 Versus  HARSALBHAI FATABHAI CHAUDHARY & 4....Respondent(s)
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: MR. H.L.JANI, APP for the Applicant(s) No. 1
MR BJ TRIVEDI, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 1 - 5  MR JT TRIVEDI, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 1 - 5
MS JIGNASA B TRIVEDI, ADVOCATE for the Respondent(s) No. 1 - 5
ORAL ORDER 1.

The present application is filed by the Applicant - State of Gujarat under Section 378 (1)(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking leave to appeal challenging the impugned judgment and order rendered in Criminal Case No. 1741 of 2011 by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Ankleshwar dated 5.2.2015 recording the acquittal of the Respondents - Original Accused for the offence under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
2. Heard learned APP Shri H.L.Jani for the Applicant State and learned Advocate Shri B.J.Trivedi for the Respondents - original accused.

3. In view of the rival submissions and having perused the record as HC-NIC Page 1 of 3 Created On Wed Sep 30 01:58:14 IST 2015 R/CR.MA/11611/2015 ORDER well as considering the reasons recorded for the findings and conclusion arrived at particularly with reference to the two reports of FSL as well as CFSL and the discussion with regard to the breach of the provisions of Section 13(2-B) read with Rule 4 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, it cannot be said that the findings and conclusion arrived at by the court below is erroneous.
The view taken is also a possible view.
Therefore, this court would decline to interfere with the findings and conclusion arrived at as this court is in broad agreement with the findings and the conclusion arrived at by the court below.

sentences.text: 1 Further, the Hon'ble Apex Court has laid down the broad guidelines with regard to approach in such acquittal appeals including the observation made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment reported in AIR 2013 SC 274 in case of Murugesan and Ors. v. State through Inspector of Police where referring to the scope of Section 378 of Cr.PC it has been observed that if the view taken by the trial court is a possible view, it cannot be disturbed merely because the other view is possible.
4. In view of the discussions made herein above, the present application deserves to be dismissed and accordingly stands dismissed.
Leave is refused.
Rule is discharged.
